question: Changing a brigade's type (common/unit_upgrades.txt), whole: the loader, CUpgradeRegimentCommand, the queue line's arithmetic, what a finished line does, the single-unit panel's list, the multi-unit path, the tooltips and the save.

addresses.name: CUpgradeRegimentCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: **Slot 6: a brigade is taken out of its unit at once and a line goes in the queue to bring its replacement.** Resolves the brigade (id +0x40/+0x44, kept at +0x3C); nothing if it is gone or has no unit (+0xB0). It tests nothing else - the condition is slot 14. New CMilitaryConstruction (0xAC bytes): line id from the counter, unit id the next number, counter moved on 3; country the brigade's owner; Size 1; target (+0x90/+0x94) the unit's id; is_reserve the brigade's (+0xA4). Strength share = min(trunc(strength * 1000 / DefaultStrength of the brigade's definition (+0x58)), 1000), or -1 where DefaultStrength is 0. A new CBrigadeConstructionDefinition (0x54 bytes) of the target type (this+0x64): id fresh from the counter (0xA9D6B0); its model is the owner's current level of each technology of the target type, in the type's own order (technologies list +0x44..+0x48 of the target definition; levels from CTechnologyStatus.level_by_technology); name the old brigade's name (slot 8), the old brigade's name released and the new one registered; experience (+0x40) = max(brigade experience (+0x3C), 0) + PRIDE_BONUS_EXP where the brigade is a pride (+0xA5); upgrading_from (+0x38) = the type looked up by the brigade definition's name in the database (0x482C80), so the database's plain type and not the brigade's technology-laden copy; upgrading_from_strength (+0x3C) = the strength share. Then manpower: menBack = trunc(GetBuildCostManpower(owner, brigade definition (+0x58), is_reserve) * share / 1000) added to Manpower (+0xBCC), floored at 0; menNew = GetBuildCostManpower(owner, the new type's built definition from MakeDefinition, is_reserve) stored in the line's manpower (+0x98) and taken off Manpower, floored at 0 - **never refused for want of men** - then CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising. builder = owner; location = the acting capital province (EnqueueConstruction zeroes it again); SetReservesFactor; RecalculateCost; EnqueueConstruction; UpdateNeeded of the production share; CUnit_AddUpgradeLine(unit, line) (0x5D3DD0); **RemoveRegimentFromUnit and CGameState::DisposeSubUnit - the old brigade ceases to exist now, not when the line ends**; for the player's own unit the interface is told (0x739BC0). Raises no message. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-upgrades.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and checked against the listing. Would be wrong if RemoveRegimentFromUnit/DisposeSubUnit were skipped on some arm - only one path reaches them, and the only returns before them are the two null checks at the top.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase_CloseUpgradeTargets
addresses.comment: **Makes the upgrade table transitive, once, after the whole of common/unit_upgrades.txt is read.** Repeats passes until one adds nothing. A pass walks the types in index order; for each type's list (its length taken before the walk, so an entry added during this pass is not walked in it) and each target j, every entry t of j's list (j's length taken at that moment, so a list only changes through later appends it does not see in this inner walk) is appended to the type's own list unless already present. **Order**: first the file's own order of that type's `upgrade` blocks, then what the passes append - which depends on the index order of the types, since a lower-indexed j was already extended earlier in the same pass and a higher one not. A cycle puts a type on its own list. No filter of the file's duplicates (the file's push_back is unconditional). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-upgrades.md.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::RecalculateCost
addresses.comment:
**Slot 14: sets a queue item's cost and duration.** It ends with exactly three stores - duration into +0x34, cost into +0x30 and a practical factor into +0xA0 - and a bare `ret`.

Two arms. Where brigades_count (+0x84) is positive and the first brigade definition has +0x38 set, the line is an upgrade of a brigade in the field: it takes the difference between the new cost and the old (floored at 0) and applies the military defines UNIT_UPGRADE_COST (+0x234), UNIT_UPGRADE_TIME (+0x238) and UNIT_UPGRADE_PRACTICAL_MOD (+0x23C).

**Otherwise, for each brigade definition**: a brigade is built on the stack and CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::MakeDefinition gives its own definition and the sum of its model's levels; `days = GetBuildTime(country, definition, levels) * 1000`; `daily = GetBuildCostIC(country, definition, levels, is_reserve)`; with more than one brigade `daily` becomes `daily * days / 1000`; the costs are added and the longest `days` kept. With more than one brigade the total is then divided by that duration. So **a unit of several brigades takes as long as its slowest and costs a day what pays for all of them over that time**, and practical_factor is 1000.

**It runs at six places, not two**: when a line is queued (CConstructUnitCommand::Execute 0x546166 and the single-unit command); on every remaining line when anything in the queue is finished (CDistributeProduction::Distribute 0x51A253); on a line going on to the next of a series (CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver 0x4851FD); on every line of a new game (CInGameIdler::Enter 0x65B76D, which then sets progress to the new duration less the old); on every line in ApplyCustomGameSettings (0x41E1E4); and **on every line of a country when any of its laws changes** (CChangeLawCommand::Execute 0x54F844). It does not run daily, so what a practical's decay does to a cost reaches a line only at one of those. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildqueue.md, section 2.

**The upgrade arm, read 2026-11-08.** MakeDefinition gives the new type's built definition and levels. icNew = GetBuildCostIC(country, it, levels, is_reserve); icOld = GetBuildCostIC(country, upgrading_from (the database's plain old type), levels, is_reserve); credit = trunc(trunc(UNIT_UPGRADE_COST * upgrading_from_strength / 1000) * icOld / 1000); cost = icNew - credit, 0 if below 1. practical_factor = 1000, or where icNew is not 0, trunc(trunc(cost * 1000 / icNew) * UNIT_UPGRADE_PRACTICAL_MOD / 1000). duration = GetBuildTime(country, new, levels) * 1000 - trunc(GetBuildTime(country, old, levels) * 1000 * UNIT_UPGRADE_TIME / 1000), 0 if below 1. The old type's cost and time are taken with the **new** type's levels. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-upgrades.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and re-read against the listing; no field meanings changed.
addresses.revises: Adds the exact arithmetic of the upgrade arm, which the entry only named.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver
addresses.comment:
**Slot 9: makes the unit a line has finished.** Bare `ret`; CDistributeProduction::Distribute calls it when progress >= duration and removes the line when it answers 1.

Answers 1 and does nothing for a country that is not REB and owns no province (owned_province_count, CCountry +0xCF8, <= 0), and for a line with no brigades. Otherwise: where accumulated_progress (+0xA8) is under 1000, adds the missing share of GetStartExperienceRate to accumulated_experience. Makes a CNavy, a CAir or a CArmy by the first brigade's type, with the line's unit id. Per brigade definition: a CShip, CWing or CRegiment with the definition's id and name; SetType; is_reserve; **experience = the greater of the definition's and accumulated_experience, capped at 100000**; the practical - the type's completion_size (+0xE4), times reserves_factor for reserves, times practical_factor (+0xA0) - through CCountry::GainTechAbility; the definition's id is incremented; the model's levels go onto the brigade's technologies by position; ApplyTechnologies; strength = max_strength * reserves_factor / 1000, no more than slot 12 allows; **organisation = GetMaxOrganisation(brigade, 1, 1), worked out before AddRegimentToUnit**, so with no officer ratio and no reserve share. Then the two accumulators are zeroed; a CUnitDeployment with id (unit type, unit id + 1) is appended to the country's deployments (+0x688) holding the unit; the line's unit id goes up by 2; a line with a target unit is joined to it. Last: `progress -= min(duration, progress)`, `size -= 1`, and where size is still above 0 slot 14 and a fresh reserves_factor. Answers `size <= 0`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildqueue.md, section 4.

**An upgrade line**, read 2026-11-08: the new brigade keeps nothing of the old beyond what Execute put on the item - the item's name (the old brigade's), experience = max(item experience, accumulated_experience) capped at 100000, is_reserve, and the model of the owner's levels at order time. Strength is the type's full default strength (times reserves_factor for a reserve) capped at GetMaxStrength, organisation GetMaxOrganisation(1, 1); it is not a pride (no such byte is set); no history is copied. Its id is the item's, minted at the order. **Joining the target** is as for any line with a target, from the listing at 0x4850A0: CUnit_CanTakeSubUnit(target, country, the new brigade, sameProvince false), or where that fails and the target is a theatre (oob_level 0), CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate(target, new unit, 0); either -> CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit(country, target, true). A target that is gone, in a battle, full or otherwise unable leaves a one-brigade unit waiting among the deployments. The last call on a finished line is the ordinary one: a name for the type's next brigade (MakeSubUnitName, registered), though the line is ending. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-upgrades.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the join condition taken from the listing at 0x4850A0-0x4850D3.
addresses.revises: Adds what an upgrade line does and the exact condition of the join.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::~CMilitaryConstruction
addresses.comment:
The destructor body (slot 0, 0x483EF0, calls it): restores the CMilitaryConstruction vftable, and where a brigade item upgrades from another type takes the line off its target unit (CUnit_RemoveUpgradeLine) - so an upgrade line finished or cancelled clears the unit's orange mark - then frees the item list. Only its head was read. Bare `ret` at 0x48402A. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 10.

**Read whole 2026-11-08.** Restores the vftable, walks the brigade items for one with upgrading_from (+0x38) set and if so CUnit_RemoveUpgradeLine(target unit, this) (the target at +0x90/+0x94 through FindPersistentByIdPair), then frees the list. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-upgrades.md.
